top_developments.headline: Take action against officials who arrested MIDS professor, Stalin urges T.N. government
top_developments.summary: CHENNAI DMK president M.K. Stalin on Saturday demanded action against police officials who had exceeded their remit by arresting Madras Institute of Development Studies (MIDS) professor Kalaiarasan. He also demanded action against the virtual miscreants whose activity had led to the arrest. Kalaiarasan was arrested over a comment on a fake ID. top_developments.headline: Tamil Nadu to set up 26 POCSO Act courts and four NDPS courts
top_developments.summary: Chennai Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has ordered the establishment of 26 courts under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, and four courts under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, to expedite the trial of cases registered under these laws. A State government press release issued on Sunday (November 1, 2026) said during a review meeting on cases registered under the POCSO Act, the Chief Minister had stressed the need to ensure justice for victims by speeding up trials.

sources.title: T.N. govt. raises DA for its employees from 60% to 63%
sources.snippet: Chennai Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Saturday announced a hike in dearness allowance (DA) for government employees and teachers with effect from July 2026. A State government press release said the DA for employees had been increased from 60% to 63%, following a similar increase for Central government employees from July 2026. The revised DA would apply to the Tamil Nadu government employees and teachers with effect from the same date.

sources.title: ‘Administrative incompetence’ characterises TVK’s reign in the State, says Palaniswami
sources.snippet: CHENNAI AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Saturday criticised the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led government for its “administrative incompetence”. Addressing a meeting in Maraimalai Nagar on the outskirts of Chennai amid the 55th formation day celebrations of his party, Mr. Palaniswami wondered what had been the achievement of the TVK-led government. Even schemes launched by it, such as the marriage assistance scheme for women, were originally implemented by the previous AIADMK regime, which had provided the financial assistance along with gold for thirumangalyam.

top_developments.headline: Pudukottai brought under heavy security cover for CM’s visit on Monday
top_developments.summary: PUDUKOTTAI Pudukottai has been brought under a heavy security cover as Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay is to visit the town on Monday to participate in a government function. Vijay’s maiden visit to Pudukottai after becoming the Chief Minister. Separate security schemes have been drafted by the Tiruchi City Police, Tiruchi Rural Police, and the Pudukottai district police as the Chief Minister is to reach Pudukottai by road from the Tiruchi International Airport. Additional strength has been drawn from other districts to tighten security in and around Pudukottai.

sources.snippet: PUDUKOTTAI With Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay scheduled to visit Pudukottai on November 2, to inaugurate the new bus stand and distribute welfare measure, semester examinations scheduled for the day at the Kalaignar Karunanidhi Government Arts College for Women, an autonomous institution in the town, has been postponed, triggering a row. The examinations in the college started on October 30 and are to conclude on November 19.

- **Madras High Court Advocates Association challenges 1965 Union Cabinet decision to continue English as common language for Supreme Court and all High Courts:** CHENNAI The Madras High Court Advocates Association (MHAA) has filed a public interest litigation petition in the High Court challenging the constitutional validity of an Union Cabinet Committee’s 1965 decision that English should continue as the common language for the Supreme Court and all High Courts in the country until it could be replaced with Hindi. First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan would be hearing the case on Monday (November 2, 2026). Regarding this, Tamil Nadu BJP leader Nayanar Nagendran said on his X page, "The news that the undertrial arrested in the robbery case in Annoor, Coimbatore has escaped for the second time after Chennai and Theni is shocking. The government continues to protect the public without properly monitoring the convict who escaped the first time... - **1,172 candidates receive offer letters at job fair held in Villupuram:** VILLUPURAM Minister for Social Justice Vanni Arasu distributed appointment orders to 1,172 job seekers at a private sector job fair held at St. Ann’s College of Arts and Science in Tindivanam on Saturday (October 31, 2026). The event was organised jointly by the Villupuram district administration, the District Employment and Career Guidance Centre, and the Tamil Nadu State Rural Urban Livelihoods Mission, under the chairmanship of District Collector Sheik Abdul Rahman. According to a press release, more than 167 companies interviewed 4,214 candidates at the fair. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/1172-candidates-receive-offer-letters-at-job-fair-held-in-villupuram/article71652132.ece))
- **Higher Education Department wants HoDs to prepare students for placement; activists cry foul:** Chennai The Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department has decided to task Heads of Departments (HoDs) of higher education institutions with the primary responsibility of preparing students for employment. Education activists, in response, have demanded a roll back stating that HoDs, who are subject experts, cannot be expected to perform the duties of placement officers. The Department’s decision was communicated to the Commissioner of Collegiate Education, Director of Technical Education, and Registrars of all universities through a letter on Friday. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/higher-education-department-wants-hods-to-prepare-students-for-placement-activists-cry-foul/article71649062.ece))
